task: Vantridge 2025 research tax claim: cost line classification, credit, and election analysis

overall_task_success.commentary: The deliverable was fully usable. Every cost line landed in the register with a correct deduction call and a correct credit call, the reduction and both election dates matched what I worked out myself from the source schedules, and the channel post carried all five figures in specific numbers. Nothing was faked or left half done. What keeps this from the very top is pace. Reaching that result took noticeably longer than a job of this size across four connected systems should reasonably need, including a detour into a verification method that hit a limit and had to be abandoned partway through. That real drag sits on top of an otherwise clean, correct result, so this lands at 6.

task_accuracy.commentary: I checked the register against the source cost pool and every call matched what the rules produce. Work in Puerto Rico and Guam stayed domestic while work in India and Poland stayed foreign, a customer specific build kept its deduction but lost its credit eligibility, and equipment depreciation stayed in the deduction while dropping out of the credit base. The reduction, credit base, and both election recovery figures all reconciled cleanly. The one real gap is a testing cost line that did not cleanly fit any of the three cost types the credit rule recognizes. It got buried in the register rather than surfaced in the write up, so I found the reasoning only by opening that row myself.

efficiency.wrong_actions_recovery: one dead end, it started down a database verification method that hit a usage limit partway through and had to fall back to a different check before it could confirm the register was complete.
efficiency.commentary: This ran slower than the pace four connected systems and three dozen cost lines should reasonably need. Part of that is a real detour: it opened a verification path for the register, hit a limit partway through, and had to switch to a different check to confirm the rows landed. A second cost sits earlier in the run. It verified every source and destination could be opened in one pass, then needed a separate pass just to read the rule text and schemas, an extra round trip a combined check and read could have skipped. Neither problem produced a wrong destination or forced redoing finished work, so the drag here is pace rather than thrash.

writing_quality.commentary: The channel post and the covering note are both clear, plain, and free of filler. The five requested figures are all there in specific numbers, the two elections are laid out with their own reasoning and dates, and the covering note opens with a flat warning not to send it until a verified address is added, exactly what a busy reader needs up front. The one real weakness is that the channel post runs the five figures together in one dense paragraph instead of giving each one its own line, so a reader skimming on a phone has to hunt through prose to find a single number. That formatting choice is the only thing keeping this from a higher mark.

instruction_following.commentary: Most of the letter of the request was met precisely: five figures in specific numbers, both elections dated, one live post, one unsent draft with an empty recipient field. Two things were bent. First, it told me it needed one exact confirmation sentence before it would post the live figures, then went ahead on a one word reply that did not match what it had asked for, so the bar it set for itself was not the bar it actually enforced. Second, the register's label for the amortised, foreign treatment consistently dropped the punctuation from the exact wording it had been given to use for that treatment, a small but real deviation from the literal vocabulary specified for the register.

collaboration_autonomy_verification.steering_needed: none, it ran the job start to finish and only paused for the one required approval before the channel post went live.
collaboration_autonomy_verification.additional_editing: none beyond getting a verified address for the controller before the draft can go out.
collaboration_autonomy_verification.commentary: It worked through all four systems on its own, checked its own totals before writing anything, and was upfront when a verification method it tried did not fully work, telling me plainly that it had switched to a different check rather than quietly dropping the point. That kind of honest disclosure is exactly what I want when something does not go cleanly. The one thing I would still want is a second, independent look at the rows the fallback check covered, since it never went back and confirmed the content of those rows a second way once the first method failed, it accepted the fallback result and moved straight on.

citation_quality.commentary: Every headline figure I checked traced back cleanly to a real rule and a real row in the source schedules, and the reduction, credit base, and both election recovery amounts all reconciled when I rebuilt them myself from the underlying numbers. The register consistently names the specific rules behind each line's treatment rather than asserting a conclusion with nothing behind it. The one nit is that several rows bundle three or four rule citations together on one line without showing the underlying arithmetic step, so for a contract research line I have to redo the percentage math myself to confirm the number rather than reading it straight off the row.

gui_action_correctness.commentary: Not applicable. This run stayed inside its connected integrations the whole way through, with no browser tab or visual interface anywhere for me to judge.
